pr_comments: So, this has all the necessary parts. However, it is still inconsistent. I would appreciate some reviews on this and recommendations on how to make it better.

I got it working consistently for inline JS. I need to run though it a few more times for the other html tests. 

I also need to add some core tests for the changes I made internally. 

**Question**
Should we do anything in this PR about the source maps?

What is the purpose of uniqueKey?

@Pytal 
uniqueKey was added to help identify the difference between the different assets that live in the same file. Prior to adding this the 4 content within the HTML page were being targeted as the same asset since fileName and type were the only used parameters to create the asset id. The asset id was used to create the content cache and when the assets were created they were all sent to the same buffer creating improper output.

How would I go about implementing this in a transformer when extracting css from js?

Would [inline handling in the html packager](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/e2ea84373758ef22da979bc7abaf9b8ca29a1f59/packages/packagers/html/src/HTMLPackager.js#L93-L122) have to be replicated in [js packager](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/packagers/js/src/JSPackager.js)?

There are two parts to it really the packager is the part that is loading it back in, but the extraction takes places in the [HTMLTransformer](https://github.com/kwelch/parcel/blob/22a3fb600ff968f2c6fb244e0ab758ccd47ff32c/packages/transformers/html/src/inline.js#L18). The advantage of HTML is that you have attributes that you can use to store the asset data for retrieval in the package. I would have to think about it further, but I am not sure of a good way to accomplish that the same way in JS.

Would it be feasible to add an addDependencyOnPackage() method?

It would infer from the bundle type how to add the add the dependency and add the dependency accordingly.

My concern is more around connecting the asset to the node in JS. With html I was able to write the ID to the HTML AST during transformer and then use it to retrieve and replace in the packager. There is no direct communication between the packager and transformer, thus you need to not only flag the asset to parcel, but also find a way to identify and connect the node on the AST to the asset that lives in parcel.

I feel that there may be a more extensible way to implement this rather than attaching a `data-parcel-id` attribute in the html tag, while also supporting other languages like js.

But for the time being the best way to implement this is to somehow add metadata to the JavaScript AST correct?

Cool, I am excited to see what that would look like. 

To make it similar to the HTML extraction that would be the next step to accomplish something in a similar way.

issue_context.title: Parcel 2: HTML Transform
issue_context.body:
Create the `@parcel/transform-html` package in `packages/transforms/html`. This package is a Parcel 2 transform plugin for HTML. It will be based on the `HTMLAsset` from Parcel 1. The main difference is that it will not be responsible for transforming with PostHTML, that will be a separate `@parcel/transform-posthtml` plugin.

The `@parcel/transform-html` package is responsible for the following things:

* Parsing with PostHTML if an AST is not already available from a previous transform.
* Collecting dependencies - e.g. images, scripts, css, etc.
* Creating sub-assets for inline scripts and styles to be processed by the pipeline, and re-inserting them back into the HTML
* Generating HTML if needed.

Just for future reference: excluding dependencies (e.g. from `src`) has these primaries use-cases:
- file will exist on a relative url in production
- preprocessing HTML for a server-used template.

The same thing occurs on `` tags. 😢 Maybe Parcel should not try to resolve dependecies from pug when it is used as plain text, putting the pipe in the beginning of the code. ```pug | Go to my resource ``` Reference: https://pugjs.org/language/plain-text.html

@reebr The trouble with that is the pug does not escape that HTML after your pipe. It simply becomes HTML. If parcel ignores it then it's not treating the HTML output uniformly, which I actually think is more confusing. If something in pug is supposed to become HTML, as is the case here, I want parcel to process it as such.

review_comments: Not sure I fully understand this change. Could you elaborate?

To compile sass we cannot give it a file because the inline data is not a file, we just have the content to conform with their API, we need to pass it as data is we have a string of content instead of file. 

The indent further down could be done better but is based on the type and that we don't have a config for inline content. The expectation is that they are setting the type of the style to sass because they want indent syntax instead of scss with block syntax.

Huh, didn't realize we weren't passing the code in all the time. Seems like it would be problematic for even normal assets for SASS to be responsible for reading the file because it won't use our virtual FS. Can revisit that later.

Perhaps we should force inline source maps for inline bundles? Looks like right now the source map just gets thrown away by the HTMLPackager, but if it were generated inline it could work. I guess we don't support inline source maps at all right now, so we could add that later.

My thought was that we would add inline later once we have support for it. 

How best can we track that? Create an issue? Throw in a `TODO`
I created #3490, feel free to beef it up with any more context that I may be missing.

This could probably be optimized to traverse the graph once at the start of packaging, and make a map of inline asset keys to bundles. This way you'd avoid re-traversing the graph for each one. Probably not a big deal, but might be nice as a future improvement.

I am good with adding this. However, it is possible we have inline bundles that are a part of a different html we are parsing, right? 

That could still be a better performance hit. 🤔
